groups.title: the local readfirst command: argument parsing, git file listing, init/prompt/check/read/diff and the agent brief

checks.why: init, check, prompt, read and diff end to end on a scratch git repository

risks.text: src/action.mjs imports repoFiles, readMapFile and readText from cli.mjs, so changing how files are listed or the map is read also changes the GitHub Action
repoFiles lists untracked files that .gitignore does not exclude, so a stray scratch file in the working tree makes `check` fail and shows up in `diff`

parse() knows its options from two lists, FLAGS (on/off) and VALUES (take a value, also as --name=value); any other --option is an error, so a new option must go into one of them or every use of it fails with 'unknown option'. Before 0.26.4 an unknown option took the next word as its value (hook --new-flag --stop ran the wrong hook). A `hook` call (not --install) never fails on its own arguments or errors: main() answers with a systemMessage warning and exit 0, because exit 2 from a PreToolUse hook refuses the tool call (an older readfirst that did not know --gate stopped every Edit and Bash call of a session, 2026-11-08)

`check` reports map problems and exits 1. prompt goes through loadMap, which settles the map as check does (settleMap) and throws (exit 2 from bin) only on what check fails on. read, diff, view, verify and export --cursor use loadMapLenient (read and diff, and the PreToolUse hook and audit, also work with no map at all: they then show only where the code broke before, from git history, and `readList` gets a null map): they only note on stderr when the map is behind the code (files in no group, patterns for deleted files) and still throw when the map is broken in itself (mapProblems with placement: false) - src/cli.mjs:168
the pattern syntax in the agent brief must match what map.mjs accepts; if you change the pattern rules, update the brief as well

runHook swallows every error and returns null (exit 0, no output), so a bug in it looks the same as 'nothing to say' and the edit goes ahead; only a test with real map data would catch it. It also uses repoFiles, readMapFile and mapProblems, so changes there change the hook. A map broken in itself (a rule naming a renamed file, bad JSON) does not silence it: both hooks open with brokenMapLine and still give what the map gives (the Stop hook blocks once with it); before 0.26.4 they said nothing for the whole repository

verify runs the map's check commands with the shell in the repository root; a map is repository content and its commands run with the user's rights, so verify stays an explicit command, never called from the PreToolUse hook or the Action. The one exception is the opt-in Stop hook (`hook --install --verify`), and it runs only commands the base branch's map already lists (trustedRuns): a command a branch adds or changes is named, never run, so checking out someone's branch cannot run their new command. On the base branch itself (main with no origin/main) trustedRuns reads the map at the last commit older than the session's first mark, never HEAD: in 0.26.4 a command the session committed to the map ran. Every file readfirst writes in the checkout (init, fix, export --cursor, verify --record, view's default page) goes through mustBeInside first, and setup through outsideRepo: a symlink that leads outside the repository stops the write. A check the Stop hook does not run blocks the stop once per state of the files (a `notrun:` mark in the hook state) and tells the agent to run `npx readfirst verify`; before 0.27.1 it passed with a note.

the MCP server answers by calling main() again with --root for each tool call, so anything a command prints to stdout becomes the tool's text; stdout is also the JSON-RPC channel, so `mcp` itself must never write anything else to stdout. `mcp` is handled before main() looks up the repository (so it starts outside a git repository): it must not use root, files or the map itself, and the repository is looked up at each tool call (--root, or git rev-parse in the current directory), where a failure comes back as an isError result 'not inside a git repository'

brokeBefore (src/history.mjs) runs one `git log` per code file for read, diff, the hook and the Action, and never throws: a missing git, a non-repository or a repository with no commits gives {} (nothing shown). A shallow clone with fewer than 200 commits gives { notFetched: true } for files with nothing to show, so a test that runs read in a `--depth 1` clone sees 'history not fetched'; a clone fetched to depth 200 or more counts as having the history

runHook and runStopHook find the repository from each edited file, not from the session's folder: a session can start in a folder above several repositories, and the hook state keeps absolute paths (older state files with relative paths still read against the session's repository). The state is append-only (readfirst-hook-<session>.lines in the temp folder, one [key, time] JSON line per marked file, written in one append): hooks of one session run at the same time, and reading and rewriting one JSON object lost the files of all but the last writer. The older .json object file is still read (readSeen) and never written. Each path is resolved through symlinks first (physical(): the nearest existing folder through realpath), because git gives the physical top level: a file reached through a linked folder (/tmp/lnk -> /tmp/x/r, or macOS /var -> /private/var) would otherwise be outside its repository and the hook silent. Looking the root up from event.cwd again would make the hook silent in that setup (rootOf finds it per file) - src/cli.mjs:458

the PreToolUse hook reads Bash commands too: src/bash-writes.mjs names the files a command writes (redirects, sed -i / perl -i, tee, cp/mv destinations, git checkout of paths, code that writes run by python/node/sh from -c, -e or a here-document: only the targets of its write calls, resolved by codeTargets from a literal, an assigned variable, a parameter, a for-loop, a glob or the script's arguments, falling back to the files it names that exist) and only those; file arguments are read per command through OPTIONS/options() in bash-writes.mjs: < and 2> redirects and option values (truncate -s N, sed -e/-f SCRIPT, cp/mv/install -t DIR, which is then the destination) are dropped first, and only -i, -i<suffix>, --in-place or a flag cluster reaching i make sed/perl write (perl -M<module>, -I<dir> do not); a command whose options are not in OPTIONS gets no option values dropped; segments split at ; && | and newlines outside quotes only, so node -e "a; fs.writeFileSync(f)" stays one command, and a here-document belongs to the last command on its line and its paths start after the cds before it; after a cd to a variable (cd $D) relative paths are not named at all; a command that merely reads or runs tests must give none, or every Bash call would carry notes. The matcher in installHook and plugins/readfirst/hooks/hooks.json includes Bash; with --gate the first call on an unseen file is denied with the notes and the retry passes, because the notes mark the file as seen. Quotes are read by blank()/closeOf(): they open again inside $( ) (so a > in python3 -c "..." inside "$(...)" is code, not a redirect, and a redirect inside $( ) is a write ending at its ); a regex once read `i>=0` there as a write to `=0`), and a quote that never closes is a plain character

Bash commands in the hook (src/bash-writes.mjs, since 0.26.5): the command is the first word after leading NAME=value words and wrappers (unwrap: sudo, env, nice, timeout, nohup, time, command, exec, ionice, stdbuf), a backslash-newline joins the lines first, `bash|sh -c '...'` strings and here-documents fed to a shell are read as commands (recursively), and gitPaths decides git checkout/restore: after `--` every word, `restore` its words, `checkout` without `--` only words that are files here (a branch or tag with a dot is not), `restore --staged` without --worktree nothing - src/bash-writes.mjs:36

src/pending.mjs reads the hosted upkeep branch (refs/remotes/*/readfirst/upkeep) from the clone's refs only, as of the last fetch (no-network-in-cli): `pending`, the MCP tool pending_map_edits and the PreToolUse hook (once per session per repository, after MIN_DAYS or MIN_MERGES) use it. The hook adds the line as context and never denies for it, even with --gate. The branch name is the hosted upkeep's: if the server renames it, this goes silent

hook state keys (src/cli.mjs): a file's absolute path (notes shown; checked at the stop), `touched:<path>` (no time left to look it up: checked at the stop, looked up on the next call), `start:<root>` (the session's first call in that repository that wrote nothing readfirst can name: the Stop hook then also checks every changed file whose mtime is newer, so a file a script wrote is not skipped), `pending:<root>` and `notrun:<root>:<state>` (the stop already blocked once for checks that did not run at this state of the files). runStopHook skips pending and notrun: a new kind of key must go into its tag list, or it is read as a file path.

the PreToolUse hook gives every file a call writes its notes, each repository's lines once (a line for only some files names them) and every line, with nothing cut (0.27.1; before, the first 10 files and 12 lines a file, and files 11 and on were never checked at the stop). It has a budget (runHook's `budget`, 10 s of the 15 s Claude Code allows): files it had no time for are named in the notes, marked `touched:` for the Stop hook and looked up on the next call; with --gate the call is refused so it is made again. Speed comes from src/hook-cache.mjs, never from leaving files or lines out.

src/hook-cache.mjs keeps the import graph and brokeBefore results per repository in the hook's state folder between calls (mode 600; a file another user owns is ignored), keyed by HEAD, the file list, the changed config files and the readfirst version. Edges from changed JS/TS/Python/JSON files are read again from the files; any other changed file (Go, C#, Java: their edges depend on other files' text) rebuilds the whole graph. A new file importEdges reads to resolve imports (beside package.json, tsconfig/jsconfig) must go into CONFIG there, or edits to it are served stale. sentry (22,494 files): 3.1 s cold, 85 ms warm, the same edges as a full rebuild.

the Stop hook counts files the session committed (git log since its first mark) as edited, and since 0.27.1 also as changed when it checks the map's `requires` (change together): `committed` takes the mark's own second (git keeps whole seconds) so no committed file goes unchecked, `committedAfter` only later seconds so a commit from before the session never stands in for a partner the session left out. Before, a pair committed together in the session (package.json and server.json) was reported as left behind.

init --agent, setup and hook --install (installHook, addAgentLine, setupAgents) add to files people edit by hand, often with comments (JSONC). A file that does not parse as plain JSON is never rewritten and never stops the rest: init goes on and prints what to add by hand (hookSnippet, SNIPPETS in src/agents.mjs). Until 0.26.4 (readfirst#130) init stopped at a .claude/settings.json with comments and wrote nothing after it. A new file that init or setup touches needs a test with a commented copy in the middle of the list.

read and diff take a file path from the repository root, from the current folder or absolute (fromHere in main): until 0.26.4 (readfirst#130) only the first worked, and `readfirst read ./x.mjs` in a subfolder said the file was not tracked. With --root (the MCP server, scripts) a relative path stays relative to the root. A new command that takes file arguments resolves them the same way; test from a subfolder and with an absolute path.

changedFiles picks what verify, diff and the Stop hook compare against: the --base given (an unknown one is an error that names it, not 'the clone is shallow': until 0.26.4 a typo in --base sent people to fetch more history), else origin/main, main, origin/master, master. On the base branch itself with no origin/<base> (changed.here) the base is HEAD: onBaseItself says only uncommitted changes are counted, and with none it fails asking for --base. Until 0.26.4 (readfirst#130) verify said 'nothing to verify' there and passed with the committed changes unchecked. An empty set of changes must never read as a pass.

No hook may fail closed on its own trouble: a hook given arguments it does not know (an older readfirst under newer settings) answers with a systemMessage and exit 0 (letThrough in main; exit 2 refused every Edit and Bash call of a session until 0.26.4, readfirst#130), and hook --gate whose state cannot be saved (a full or read-only temp folder: addSeen throws) passes the notes as context instead of refusing (until 0.27.0, readfirst#133, every retry was refused again). Test with an unknown option and with an unwritable state folder.

bin/readfirst.mjs ends the process quietly when stdout or stderr is closed early (EPIPE: `readfirst read x | head -1`); until 0.26.4 (readfirst#130) that crashed with a stack trace and exit 1. The handler rethrows every other error, and nothing in src may install a handler that swallows them.

groups.title: the GitHub Action: one PR comment with the read list for the changed files, and a failed check when the map falls behind

checks.why: the Action against a fake GitHub API: post, update in place, broken map, read-only token, non-PR events, auto-fix commits

risks.text: composite actions do not set INPUT_* env vars, so action.yml maps each input to an env var by hand; a new input needs a line in action.yml and a read in action.mjs
the existing PR comment is found by its first line (MARKER); changing MARKER makes every open PR get a second comment instead of an update
a 403 from a comment write is treated as a fork PR and swallowed by matching ': 403 ' in the message built by api(); changing that error text turns fork PRs into failed jobs
the script runs only when argv[1] ends with '/src/action.mjs', and action.yml calls it by that path; moving or renaming the file makes the Action exit successfully without doing anything
when the map has problems the comment shows the problems but no read list, and the job fails unless fail-on-map-problems is 'false'

auto-fix writes to the PR branch through the contents API: only on a branch of this repository (never a fork), only when the branch's map equals the one this run read (else it would overwrite a newer push), and only what settleMap settles; anything a person must decide stays in the comment

the changed files still come from the GitHub API, but the 'Files in this PR that broke before' section reads the checkout's git log (brokeBefore) and says 'history not fetched (set fetch-depth: 200 on actions/checkout)' when the checkout is shallow; the workflow `init --ci` writes and this repository's ci.yml both set fetch-depth: 200, so keep the three in step

the Action's PR comment and `diff` render a judged read list with toMarkdown(..., { verdict }) (0.29.0): the verdict (src/verdict.mjs) first, then the rules and risks the change touches, then those it could not match (risks whose own files name a changed file open, group-wide ones folded), then the rest folded with their counts (not triggered, hot spots, flows, vocabulary, tests, users, broke before). The checks, change-together, being-replaced and other-repository rows are in the verdict and not listed again. toMarkdown returns before the plain layout when given a verdict, so a new section added to the plain layout is missing from diff and the PR comment unless verdictMarkdown shows it too (VERDICT_PLACES and its test catch a new list of the read list, not a new section of an old one). `read` and --json keep the plain layout. A risk is `named` only when it has `files`; a map whose risks carry no files gets every unmatched risk folded

action.yml runs `node` itself (composite): a self-hosted runner without Node gets a clear ::error:: from the `command -v node` guard instead of 'command not found'; the Action does not set up Node, because actions/setup-node would change the Node of the user's later steps

a read list longer than one comment is split by splitComment (60,000 characters a part, cut only between top-level blocks; a <details> block is closed and reopened with '(continued)'); part N starts with partMarker(N), `<!-- readfirst:pr-comment:N -->`, and is found by it on the next push, as part 1 is by MARKER. Changing partMarker gives every open PR new parts; the job summary gets the whole body unsplit.

The Action finds its comment by the first line (MARKER; partMarker(N) for the parts of a long one) and edits it in place. Anyone can post a comment that starts with the marker: until 0.26.5 (readfirst#132, security) another user's such comment was taken as ours, the PATCH failed with 403, the 403 was read as a fork PR, and no readfirst comment was posted. Bots' marked comments are tried first, then the rest newest first, each PATCH that fails with 403 or 404 moves to the next, and a new comment is posted only when none can be edited. Test with a marked comment by another user.

groups.title: the map format and checker, the first-draft map, import reading (JS/TS, Python and seven more languages) and the read list

checks.why: patterns, draft, check messages, imports and read list cases

risks.text: mapProblems rejects unknown fields, so a new map field must be added to the allowed-field list and made optional, and older readfirst versions will reject maps that use it; maps in users' repositories must keep passing under readfirst/map@1
the read list object is the --json output and what the Action renders; keep its field names and the readfirst/read-list@1 format string
patternToRegExp is used for group files, ignore, rule files and risk files alike; changing what a pattern matches moves files between groups in every user's map

test files are recognised by two separate regexes (isTest in readlist.mjs, which covers every language langs.mjs reads, and the top-level tests-folder check in draftMap); a new test naming convention goes into isTest, and into draftMap only if it is a top-level folder

imports are read with regexes: JS/TS and Python in imports.mjs, Go, Rust, Elixir, C#, Java/Kotlin, Ruby and PHP in langs.mjs. Only edges that resolve to a tracked file count (workspace packages, tsconfig paths aliases and baseUrl, package.json #imports, and Python roots at each folder with manage.py, pyproject.toml, setup.py or setup.cfg included), so packages from outside, aliases set up elsewhere (bundler config, tsconfig extends) and names the approximation misses (Rails constants used unqualified inside a module, C# types reached without a using) leave tests out of the read list

readlist.mjs and settleMap (map.mjs) read fixMap's change messages (`groups.<id>: added <pattern>`): readlist for the 'would add it to group' hint, settleMap to tell a new top-level folder from a file beside placed ones; rewording those messages silently breaks both

labels are personal: they live in .readfirst/local/, which keepLocal adds to .git/info/exclude; reading labels from anywhere else, or writing them into the map, would hand one person's notes to the whole team
the view page loads three.js 0.160.0 from cdn.jsdelivr.net through an import map; without network it shows only the WebGL/connection notice

the view page only has interface strings for en and ko, and the language switch only toggles between them: a labels file for any other language (e.g. `prompt --labels ja`) is read and inlined but never shown, and the plain/technical switch appears only when the current language's file has "plain"

check, read, diff, verify and the Action settle a map that is only behind the code the way fix would (settleMap) and pass; only what fix cannot place, broken rules and new top-level folders fail. Making them strict again breaks every PR that adds a file

audit's 'hot spots nothing checks' counts a group check as a check of its own only if fewer than half the groups share the same `run` string (always, if the map has under two groups). Adding one command such as `npm test` to most groups, or writing the same check with different text, changes which hot spots are listed. A rule check only counts when the rule's files cover the hot spot's file. - src/audit.mjs:109

readfirst's own files (the map, .readfirst/held.json and the exported .cursor/rules/readfirst-*.mdc) belong to no group: isOwnFile in map.mjs (OWN_FILES and OWN_PATTERN) keeps them out of placement, and readlist.mjs reports them as status MAP. A new file readfirst writes into the checkout must be added there, or check fails with it as an unplaced file. The Cursor file name is matched twice (OWN_PATTERN in map.mjs and isCursorExport in export.mjs): change both together. The text export writes is compared byte for byte by `export --cursor --check`, so rewording it makes every user's CI fail until they re-export. - src/map.mjs:10

the agents setup knows are listed in several places: AGENTS, detectAgents, PLAN and SNIPPETS in src/agents.mjs, the notes-file list in addAgentLine (cli.mjs), the HELP text and the 'Wire every agent at once' section of docs/guide.md. A new agent must be added to all of them: without a PLAN entry setupAgents throws on it, and without a SNIPPETS entry the by-hand message for an unparsable file says only 'the readfirst MCP server'. Setup writes a file only when it parses as plain JSON (or, for Codex, when no [mcp_servers.readfirst] table exists), and a readfirst key that is already there is never compared or updated.

src/shapes.mjs and src/lex.mjs are copied from readfirst-cloud lib/discarded.mjs and lib/lex.mjs with only the published shapes kept (queryset, str-method, str-replace, js-string, js-replace, js-expect-promise); do not add the server's other shapes here, they stay hosted. js-expect-promise leaves out files on vitest or bun test (notIn: a *.vitest.* name or an import of vitest or bun:test), which fail such a test themselves; keep notIn the same on both sides

the scar rules in src/history.mjs (SIGNALS, NOISE, NOT_CODE, TEST, scar, spreadScars) are a copy of the hosted version's lib/history.mjs, kept in one module so the hosted side can import them from the package; a change to the regexes or weights changes what `read`, `diff`, the Action and `audit` call a scar, and the threshold constants (MIN_WEIGHT 2 for a file, BROKE_MOST_MIN_SCORE 2 with BROKE_MOST_MIN_COMMITS 2 for audit) decide when a young repository shows nothing; NOT_TRAP only trims the audit ranking

flows have no count limit since 0.25.0 (OLD_MAX_FLOWS 500 before): the map stores every path, and a reader caps only its own work. A map with more than 500 flows fails a CLI before 0.25.0, so pins.mjs FIELD_SINCE warns in `check` when the pinned readfirst is older, and the server must not write more than 500 for such a pin

a target that is not tracked (deleted in the change, or new and not added) keeps status NOT_TRACKED and its 'not a tracked file' note, but readList still gives it its group's checks, risks and deprecation, and the rules, requires and dependents entries that match its path: verify, diff and the Action (which passes removed files too) rely on this so a change made only of deletions still runs its group's checks. It gets no tests or unseen entries; since 0.27.0 its users are listed, from import edges built over the tracked files plus the targets (edgesWith), with a 'still imported by' note, and a target that settling left in no group is looked up in the map as written (`before`). - src/readlist.mjs:102

readList lists every test and direct user unless a limit is passed (`read --limit`, the Action's `limit` input), and `truncated` says how many a limit cut. No caller passes a limit of its own any more (the hook passed 10, view 5 and the Action 30 before 0.27.1, and view counted the five as all the users): a new caller that cuts a list must say what it cut.

the hooks keep importEdges' result between calls (src/hook-cache.mjs): edges from a changed JS/TS/Python/JSON file are read again from that file alone, with the config files in its CONFIG (package.json, tsconfig/jsconfig, pyproject.toml, setup.py, setup.cfg). A resolver that starts reading another file, or edges of those languages that come to depend on other files' text, must be added there, or the hook serves stale edges until the next commit.

bashWrites (src/bash-writes.mjs) is a hand-written shell reader, and every syntax it misses is a write the PreToolUse hook gives no notes for and, unless the file changed after the session's first mark, the Stop hook does not check; every syntax it misreads as a write puts notes on a command that only reads. Both have happened: &> and &>> (0.26.4); quotes not opening again inside $( ), so i>=0 in python -c became a write to =0 (0.26.4); NAME=val, sudo/env/nice/timeout wrappers, backslash-newline and bash -c strings (0.26.5, readfirst#132); a branch or tag with a dot and restore --staged read as writes (0.26.5); 2> and >|, (cd d && ...), pushd, globs and ~ missed, and (( x > 0 )), # comments, patch -p 1, remote or dry-run rsync read as writes (0.27.0, readfirst#133); a cd inside ( ) carried on past its ), so the hook showed another repository's notes, the ) stuck to the last word (`f.txt)`) and a redirect after the ) went into the subshell's folder (0.27.4: parens() in bash-writes.mjs; a { } group keeps its cd, as the shell does). Still missed (2026-11-09): a write inside an awk program (print ... > file). A new case needs a test of the written form and one of the look-alike that only reads.

Every file readfirst writes in a user's checkout goes through a check that the real path stays inside the repository: mustBeInside (src/cli.mjs: init, fix, export --cursor, verify --record, view) or outsideRepo (src/agents.mjs: setup, hook --install). A CLAUDE.md, .claude, .cursor or .github that is a symlink to a place outside would otherwise be written through, into the user's home or another project (setup until 0.26.4, readfirst#130; export, init, fix and view until 0.26.5, readfirst#132, security). A new write, or a new file setup or export touches, needs the same check and a test with a symlinked folder and a symlinked file.

JSON a user wrote (the map, package.json, tsconfig, .claude/settings.json, the event file) may start with a UTF-8 byte order mark that npm and editors accept and JSON.parse does not: until 0.26.4 (readfirst#130) such a map failed as 'not valid JSON'. Read user files through readText (src/cli.mjs) or unBom (src/map.mjs); a JSON.parse straight on readFileSync of a user file is the bug. A new file read needs a test with a BOM.

find (src/find.mjs) knows definitions only through its line regexes (DEFS): a declaration shape none of them matches is absent from `readfirst find`, and an agent writes the function again. Missed until 0.27.0 (readfirst#133): class methods, exports.x = and module.exports.x =, arrows wrapped in a call or with generics, abstract and declared classes. A new language or syntax goes into DEFS with a test of the declaration and of a line that only looks like one (a call, a string, a comment).

draftChecks and workspaceChecks (src/map.mjs) write commands into the user's map, and verify and the Stop hook later run them in a shell with the user's rights. A drafted check must only read (no lint --fix, prettier --write, jest -u or --updateSnapshot: REWRITES), end by itself (no watch script: vitest without run, jest --watch, a dev server: WATCHES; verify hung until 0.26.4), use the project's runner (poetry run pytest, uv run pytest; a Makefile test := is a variable, not a target), and quote every package name, folder or script name read from the repository (pnpm --filter 'a; touch x' ran touch x until 0.26.5, readfirst#132, security). codexConfig (src/agents.mjs) must not write a second [mcp_servers.readfirst] table (0.27.0). A new drafted check needs a test with a hostile name and with a script that writes or watches.

A group risk with `files` shows for those files in any group (risksNaming in src/map.mjs, used by readList, audit, view and export --cursor; 0.27.2). Before, only the file's own group was read, so a risk naming a file of another group showed for no file and check passed. unshownRisks lists risks whose text names a tracked file that does not show them: `about` (named in the first clause, before the first : ; , or '. ') is listed first and fails check --strict; a later mention is listed after and never fails. A new reader of group risks must go through risksNaming, or cross-group risks go unseen there again.

setup --git (src/git-hooks.mjs) writes the hooks git runs: `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` (.git/hooks, core.hooksPath, the main repository's .git/hooks for a worktree), and for husky (core.hooksPath .husky/_ or .husky) the user's .husky/<hook>, never husky's own _ folder. It adds one line and never replaces a hook; a hooks folder outside the repository and its git folder (a global core.hooksPath shared by every repository), a hook file that is a link out of them, a hook that hands over with exec (the pre-commit framework's: a line after it never runs) and one that is not a shell script are printed for adding by hand. The hooks call `npx --yes readfirst check` and `verify`, so they need the map (setup --git refuses without one) and npx at commit time; check reads the working tree, so an untracked file that is not ignored blocks a commit until the map places it. A new hook or a new hook manager needs a test of where it writes and of what it leaves alone (test/setup-git.test.mjs).

src/trigger.mjs judges each risk and rule of a change's read list (judge, used by `diff` and the Action, not by `read`): what it is about is the backticked names and the code-looking names (camelCase, snake_case, UPPER_CASE with _) declared in the files it is shown for, the files its text names or the changed files, plus its path:line evidence, which is carried from the file before the change to where it is now (toNew, from the hunk headers). Triggered when a changed line falls in that declaration (to its own closing brace, or in Python its indent; else up to the next declaration less the blank and comment lines above it) or the name is in an added or removed line of code (not in docs, the map, config, comments or strings: on its own PR the map edit and trigger.mjs's comments named runHook and changedFiles); a plain lowercase word counts only as a function in the item's own files and never by appearing in the diff (a test's own `run` helper and the word `files` made risks read as touched on readfirst#139). An item naming nothing found is triggered by its files, as before, and a not-triggered one is listed with its reason, never dropped. Evidence that has drifted from its code (src/cli.mjs:266 pointed into verifyChecks for a risk about rootOf until 0.28.0) gives a wrong verdict: check the line when a risk reads as triggered or not for no reason.

src/verdict.mjs writes the verdict from the read list by template, in en or ko (T): every count it gives must be of rows shown below it, and every line a reader must act on (blocked, to do) must come from a row, never from a guess. A new kind of row the verdict should count goes into sortRows or verdictLines and into every language of VERDICT_TEXT: a string in `en` alone would throw for `ko` at render time (t.x is not a function), and test/verdict.test.mjs fails on a language missing a key. The language is `diff --lang`, else the one verdict language among this clone's labels (diffLang in src/cli.mjs), else en; the Action reads the `language` input. An unknown code is said in the verdict and the job log, never silently English. Only the template is translated: the map's text is never machine-translated here (no-network-in-cli, no model)

groups.title: node:test suites for the command, the map, imports, the read list and the Action

risks.text: npm test only runs test/*.test.mjs, so a test in a subfolder or with another file name never runs
the CLI tests create and commit to real git repositories in the temp folder, so git must be on PATH
fakeGitHub answers any write it does not recognise with success, so a new GitHub API call in action.mjs passes unless a test asserts it
the tests assert exact markdown strings and draft group ids, so rewording toMarkdown or changing draftMap means updating these assertions and the README example
the hook test calls main(['hook']) without a stateDir, so it writes to the real temp folder and relies on a unique session_id; reusing a fixed id would make the hook print nothing on later runs

test/silent-cuts.test.mjs finds cuts by their shape, not by meaning: a slice to a number, an UPPER_CASE constant or max/limit/count, a slice from the end (.slice(-N), N of 3 or more or a constant; missed until 0.27.4, so verify's last-30-lines cut passed), a push under such a bound, a loop stopped at one. A cut of text is told apart by its receiver (sha, hash, title, subject, message, body, String(), a string method): a list named like one of those, or a cut to a bound of another name (k, at, end), is not looked at. When it misses one, widen the shapes; do not add a cut: note to pass it

groups.title: package manifest, README, license and CI

risks.text: package.json "files" decides what npm ships (bin, src, README.md); a new folder under src ships automatically, a new top-level folder the command needs must be added there
CI's readfirst job runs this checkout's own Action (uses: ./), so every PR fails when a new file is not in .readfirst/map.json or when src/action.mjs is broken

docs/guide.md repeats the command list, the Action inputs table and a sample read list, and README.md the three start commands; update them when cli.mjs HELP, action.yml inputs or toMarkdown output change

server.json lists readfirst in the official MCP Registry (mcp-registry.yml, after a release is published and npm shows the version); its version and packages[0].version must equal package.json's version (and package-lock.json's two version fields: run `npm install --package-lock-only` after bumping), and its name must equal package.json's mcpName, or the release or the listing fails (bump all three together). docs/guide.md also pins the release version twice (`npx readfirst@X.Y.Z` and the Action's `@vX.Y.Z`); update both on every version bump or the guide tells people to pin an old release

plugins/readfirst is listed twice: in .agent-marketplace.json (Paradev, with version) and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (Claude Code). Its version lives in plugins/readfirst/plugin.json, plugins/readfirst/.claude-plugin/plugin.json and the .agent-marketplace.json entry; change all three together, and a Paradev release is the git tag readfirst@<version>, so bump the version instead of moving a tag - .agent-marketplace.json:18

To try an older readfirst (to reproduce a report against a past commit), use a git worktree: `git worktree add <scratch dir> <commit>` and run `node <scratch dir>/bin/readfirst.mjs` there, then `git worktree remove` it. Never check out an old commit in this working checkout: its Claude Code hooks (.claude/settings.json, and a session's hooks above the repositories) run this checkout's bin/readfirst.mjs, so a commit that does not know an option the settings pass (--gate before 0.23.0) refused every Edit and Bash call, including the checkout that would have undone it (2026-11-08). From 0.26.4 a hook that fails on its own arguments warns and lets the call through, but older commits still refuse.

.claude/settings.json and CLAUDE.md call this checkout's bin/readfirst.mjs (`node "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/bin/readfirst.mjs" hook` and `hook --stop`), because `npx readfirst` does not resolve inside its own package. Running `hook --install` here would overwrite them with `npx readfirst` commands that fail, and so would `setup` or `init --agent`, which now call the same installHook as soon as they see `.claude/` or CLAUDE.md. If bin/readfirst.mjs moves, or the hook, read, find or verify commands are renamed, update both files. - .claude/settings.json:9

plugins/readfirst calls the CLI by command name: SKILL.md runs `readfirst read`, `find`, `verify`, `check` and `init --agent`, and hooks/hooks.json runs `readfirst hook` through `npx --yes`. Renaming or removing one of these commands in cli.mjs breaks the plugin for every agent that installed it, so update SKILL.md and hooks.json together with HELP. - plugins/readfirst/skills/readfirst/SKILL.md:18

README.md links to docs/guide.md by absolute GitHub URL because npm ships only README.md (package.json "files"); a relative link such as docs/guide.md or ../docs/... works on GitHub but is dead on the npm page, so keep links from the README to the guide absolute

every release published on GitHub fires major-tag and mcp-registry, including the plugin's (readfirst@X.Y.Z); both jobs run only for v-tags (or by hand), or a plugin release on the same commit moves nothing and lists the same server.json version first, failing the CLI release as a duplicate (v0.23.0 with readfirst@0.2.0). mcp-registry treats 'cannot publish duplicate version' as done - .github/workflows/mcp-registry.yml:14

groups.title: example maps for public repositories, with sample read output

risks.text: each example names the commit it was made at; regenerate the sample output when the read format changes

rules.rule: the readfirst command reads only the checkout: no network calls, no model calls, no API key (src/pending.mjs reads the clone's refs as of the last fetch, never fetches)
rules.why: it runs in agents' sandboxes and on private code; only the Action talks to the GitHub API

rules.rule: no runtime dependencies: Node's standard library only
rules.why: npx readfirst must start fast and nothing third-party runs on users' code

rules.rule: every tracked file is in exactly one group or in ignore, except readfirst's own files (the map, .readfirst/held.json and the exported .cursor/rules/readfirst-*.mdc, see isOwnFile), and every group and rule pattern matches a tracked file; check fails otherwise
rules.why: this is what stops the map from quietly falling behind the code; the exported Cursor files must not need a group, or committing them would fail check --strict

rules.rule: maps written for readfirst/map@1 keep passing: never rename or remove a map field or make an optional one required without a new format version
rules.why: map.json files live in users' repositories and CI fails on any map problem

rules.rule: the read list JSON keeps its field names under readfirst/read-list@1
rules.why: agents and tools read `readfirst read --json` and `diff --json`

rules.rule: only `readfirst init`, `readfirst setup`, `readfirst fix`, `readfirst hook --install` and `readfirst view` write files in the checkout: init writes the map (never over an existing one without --force) and, with --agent, does what setup does, and with --ci .github/workflows/readfirst.yml (never over an existing one); setup --git adds one line to the pre-commit and pre-push hooks inside the repository or its git folder (src/git-hooks.mjs); setup adds the read-first line to agent notes files and readfirst's entry to the project's own agent configs (.claude/settings.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json, .gemini/settings.json, .codex/config.toml, opencode.json), keeping what is there and never rewriting a file it cannot parse, and never writes outside the checkout (the user's home folder is printed, not written); fix writes only the map; hook --install writes only .claude/settings.json and keeps what is already there; view writes only under .readfirst/local/ (the page) and adds one line to this clone's .git/info/exclude, never anything git tracks; the plain `hook` writes only its state file and its cache (src/hook-cache.mjs) in the temp folder; `hook --stop` writes only a line in that state file (the checks it said did not run) and runs only the base branch's check commands, like verify; check, prompt (with or without --labels), read, diff, find, audit, scan, pending and the mcp server never change the checkout; export --cursor writes and removes only .cursor/rules/readfirst-*.mdc; verify writes nothing itself except, with --record, .readfirst/held.json (which rules held, at which commit), and only runs the commands the map lists, which may write as they would when run by hand; the Action writes nothing in the checkout, and with auto-fix only commits the map that fix would write to the PR branch through the API
rules.why: agents run read and diff freely before every change, and the hook runs before every edit, so it must not touch the working tree

rules.rule: the Action keeps one comment per PR, plus one more for each 60,000 characters a long read list needs, and edits them in place on each push; a part a longer list left behind is emptied with a line saying so, never deleted, and nothing in the comment is cut
rules.why: a new comment on every push floods the PR, and a comment cut short hides what the map says (it was cut at 60,000 characters until 0.27.1)

rules.rule: a read-only token (PR from a fork) must not fail the Action: the read list goes to the job summary instead
rules.why: contributors from forks would otherwise get a red check they cannot fix

rules.rule: the Action takes the PR's changed files from the GitHub API, not from git history
rules.why: actions/checkout defaults to a shallow clone, so any checkout depth must work

rules.rule: the public code holds no hosted-version logic: the prompts and steps that fill the map stay on the server
rules.why: the free code is MIT and public; the paid value is the server's judgement. The hosted design lives in the private readfirst-cloud repository.

rules.rule: nothing readfirst finds is cut to look shorter: a list cut to a fixed size for output (slice(0, N), a count that stops a loop) names the rest or says where it is, in a `cut:` comment on that line or the one above
rules.why: the owner's rule (2026-11-09): no bug hidden, no check skipped; fourteen silent cuts were found in two days, each hiding files, tests, lines or findings

checks.why: every fixed-size cut of a list carries a cut: comment

requires.why: the MCP registry workflow publishes server.json, whose versions must match package.json
the guide's "Wire every agent at once" section lists what setup writes for each agent

dependents.why: the hosted server imports src/map.mjs from the readfirst version pinned in its package.json; a new map field reaches the server only after a release and a bump of that pin, so the server must not write it before then
the fill sandbox runs a copy of the CLI named by vendor/readfirst/VERSION; paying users get the old CLI until it is copied again
src/shapes.mjs is the published subset of the server's bug shapes; a fix to one of these shapes on either side belongs on both
src/history.mjs holds the scar rules the hosted version keeps a copy of (lib/history.mjs); a change to a regex or weight on either side belongs on both
